text:
devsec-bot: ALERT detected: GCS bucket 'redwood-secrets-backups' has binding to 'allAuthenticatedUsers' with roles/storage.objectViewer and roles/storage.objectCreator. scanner: iam-policy-scan-4.
pranav: :eyes: copying findings to thread. which project?
devsec-bot: project=redwood-backups-prod, bucket=redwood-secrets-backups, first-seen=1842109600, rule=gcs-public-iam-binding, severity=high
tanya: omg that's the nightly backup bucket. can someone confirm whether retention has copies of credentials?
ashley: pulling audit logs now. running: `gcloud logging read "resource.type=storage_bucket AND protoPayload.methodName: 'SetIamPolicy'" --project=redwood-backups-prod --limit=50`
lee: I see a SetIamPolicy by CI-SA@redwood-prod. Timestamp 1842109589. Principal appears to be a CI service account, not an external user. but the policy included allAuthenticatedUsers — probably from a borked templated terraform module.
pranav: copy the policy blob and remove the binding immediately. I'll run containment.
pranav: `gcloud storage buckets remove-iam-policy-binding gs://redwood-secrets-backups --member=allAuthenticatedUsers --role=roles/storage.objectViewer --project=redwood-backups-prod`
ops-oncall: applied. response: binding removed. :white_check_mark:
ashley: confirming object access: `gsutil ls gs://redwood-secrets-backups` now returns AccessDenied for anonymous users. good.
lee: we should also disable the CI job that created the policy to prevent reapply. which pipeline is that?
ashley: looks like ci/backups/terraform-apply in buildkite; trigger principal is CI-SA. I've paused the pipeline.
anya: (joining) suggest rotating any SA keys used by that pipeline and revoking tokens.
pranav: agreed. creating new key and rotating creds. Also adding a deny policy to forbid allAuthenticatedUsers on any bucket in the org as a guardrail.
pranav: `gcloud org-policies allow orgpolicy-gcp-disallow-public-buckets` (placeholder) — will file request with infra to push org-policy.
lee: audit note: check object listings between 1842109000-1842109600 to see if any data was exfiltrated. ashley can you pull access logs?
ashley: pulling StorageAccessLogs and VPC flow logs. grep for anonymous or external IPs. quick note: there were ~12 GET requests from 52.14.100.23 during that window. Looks like listing attempts.
ops-oncall: escalate to incident channel? I'd like legal/cust-sec looped if credentials are in backups.
pranav: yes creating incident INC-2026-019 and pinging customer-security and legal. adding initial severity=high, impact=potential credential exposure in backup artifacts.
lee: remediation checklist: 1) removed allAuthenticatedUsers binding (done) 2) paused terraform pipeline (done) 3) rotate SA keys (in progress) 4) scan bucket contents for secrets and run selective rekey if found 5) enable uniform bucket-level access + retention 6) org-policy deny public bindings 7) postmortem and commit to infra templates
ashley: scanning objects with `gcloud alpha storage ls --all` and then running secrets detector. found 2 files matching regex of private keys `(?i)(-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----)` in backups/old/2025-11-01.tar.gz.
pranav: who had access to those files? looks like the backup job may have included sensitive dirs. we need to assume compromise until proven otherwise.
ops-oncall: notifying CS and infra on-call. sending incident notification to #incidents and #legal.
lee: action owner list: pr anav=containment + key rotation, ashley=forensics + logs, tanya=customer comms & legal, lee=postmortem + infra template fixes.
pranav: timeline note: detected 1842109600, binding created 1842109589, removal 1842110005, pipeline paused 1842110050.
tanya: drafting customer-facing template now. will avoid technical details, promise investigation and timelines.
ashley: exporting logs to secure bucket for SRE forensic analysis: `gcloud logging sinks create redwood-forensic-1842109876 storage.googleapis.com/redwood-forensic-logs --log-filter='resource.type=storage_bucket' --project=redwood-backups-prod`
pranav: next steps: rotate SA keys, revoke any long-lived keys, scan all backups for secrets, remediate infra templates, apply org-policy block, and schedule an incident review within 48h.
ops-oncall: good job. adding postmortem milestone to tracking board. :thumbsup:
pranav: will follow up with a short runnable remediation PR for terraform module by EOD.
lee: please add any IOCs (IPs, timestamps, file names) to the incident ticket.
pranav: done. closing thread for now — tracking in INC-2026-019.
